lens: Reversibility — revert cost, data loss, rollback runbook
answer: git revert of the merge commit is clean. All 44 changed files are in-repo source/doc/registry artifacts with no external system side-effects. The five ADR amendments are single-line path substitutions (product-control/capabilities/ -> registry/capability-templates/); a revert restores them atomically. The six .omc/.project-memory.json.tmp.<UUID> stowaways were modified (not deleted) by the PR, so they survive in git history and are recoverable via git checkout <pre-merge-sha> -- <path>; data_loss_class = none. The v1+v2 coexistence (capability-record-template.yaml and capability-record-template-v2.yaml both updated to the new path) creates mild rollback ambiguity: if an in-flight Foundry invocation resolved its template path from registry/capability-templates/ at call entry and git revert lands while that call is executing, the runtime will 404 on the path until it retries. This is a transient window, not a data-loss event, because no state is written to the old path during the PR — the YAML files are read-only fixtures. The registry/artifact-capabilities-registry.json addition of 105 lines is the only net-new artifact; a revert removes those rows cleanly with no orphaned references because the capability gates re-derive their paths from that registry at startup.
key_claims: git revert <merge-commit> restores all 44 files atomically; no external system (cluster, DB, queue) was mutated by this PR
Five ADR amendments are single-line path substitutions; revert is exact inverse with no semantic loss
Six .omc/.tmp.<UUID> files were MODIFIED not deleted; blobs exist in git object store and are fully recoverable
v1+v2 template coexistence creates a narrow in-flight-call ambiguity (path resolved at call entry vs. post-revert), but no data is written to the template path so no data loss occurs
105-line registry addition in artifact-capabilities-registry.json reverts cleanly; downstream gates re-derive paths at startup so no stale pointer survives
uncertainty_areas: Whether any running Foundry agent has the old product-control/capabilities/ path cached in memory at revert time — not observable from diff alone
Whether CI lane lean-a-foundry-capability-template-registry is gated on merge-back to dev after a revert, or whether the revert itself would need to re-trigger that lane
revert_steps: 1. git revert <merge-commit-sha> — restores all 44 files including 5 ADR path refs and 3 git-mv'd capability YAMLs atomically
2. Verify no in-flight Foundry calls are active (check observability dashboard for capability-template path resolutions) before issuing the revert to avoid the transient 404 window
3. Verify: grep -rn 'registry/capability-templates' docs/decisions/ returns 0 hits after revert
4. Verify: cargo run -p oya-dev-cli -- gate validate foundry-capability-schema exits 0 (confirms CLI path constant reverted correctly in crates/oya-dev-cli/src/lib.rs)
5. To recover any .omc/.project-memory.json.tmp.<UUID> if accidentally re-removed: git log --all --full-history -- .omc/<filename>, then git checkout <sha> -- .omc/<filename>

findings.summary: v1+v2 template coexistence (capability-record-template.yaml and capability-record-template-v2.yaml) means a reverter must update two files to restore the canonical path, not one. The PR correctly updated both, but no rollback note documents this dual-file requirement.
findings.recommended_action: Add a one-line comment in each template header citing the sibling file so a future reverter knows to update both in lockstep.

findings.summary: Six .omc/.project-memory.json.tmp.<UUID> stowaways are ephemeral agent scratch files committed alongside the functional change. If these are re-removed by a cleanup pass after a revert, they cannot be recovered without git archaeology. Their presence in the PR diff is noise that makes revert surface area appear larger than it is.
findings.recommended_action: Add .omc/*.tmp.* to .gitignore to prevent future stowaways; no action needed for reversibility of the current PR.
